inspection: D4, D5 and D6.1–D6.3 outcomes were inspected. The following variants, populations, features and comparisons are specified before their predictive scoring; not blinded preregistration.
population: Exactly D6.3's authenticated 34 scoped graphs, 450/450/60 target rows, magnitudes, normalized ranks and 5/5/9 groups. No outcome-dependent rescoping, receiver deletion, reranking, graph weighting, anatomy substitution or study pooling. Dataset8 remains outside this profile.
providerMass: Explicit synthetic unit edge masses in a source-bound analysis carrier, not measured biological weights. Unit provider lengths are 1; inverse-target-share lengths are the scoped target in-degree. The full provider context is precisely the already selected scoped graph, never its parent anatomy.
geometry: Keep the 31-coordinate D3 pair layout and unit Forman. Static O is directed transport curvature at the declared provider metric after shortest-endpoint closure and mean-one normalization; idleness affects both static O and flow. The terminal flow fields and stopping rule remain D3. Static O keeps the provider metric when only initial lengths change. This is transport-metric sensitivity, not weighted Forman or a new distance API; no interval midpoints.
initialization: Provider variants initialize flow with provider lengths. The shape variant uses 1+out-degree(source) on every scoped edge; the scale control uses 2 on every edge. Both preserve unit static O. Existing exact closure and mean-one normalization precede iteration zero.
learner: Reuse D3 weighted ridge, train-only transforms, five penalties, exact ties and identical nested whole-group splits. Refit both geometry models for every available variant/study. B and B+S are unchanged authenticated D6.3 controls, reused with disclosed costs. Q is outside this sensitivity, not selected by its score.
primaryWithinSecondaryStudy: Geometry gain over the fixed expanded graph baseline, separately for every declared variant and study. Retain all alternatives and reference differences; no winner selection or parameter tuning across variants. One-factor studies do not cover interactions or arbitrary idleness values.
aggregation: Equal intervention means within groups, then equal group means. Exact rational differences from integer rank-skill counts determine signs. Retain D3 binary64 means and descriptive group/leave-one-group-out ranges; these are not confidence intervals or significance tests.
coverage: A variant/study requires every original prepared scoped graph in its domain, including non-target-bearing Dataset7 roots, and all original target groups. A declared geometry limit makes that whole variant/study unavailable with null comparisons; continue and retain every scope attempt and all other variants. Never fit a surviving subset. Unexpected integrity/runtime errors and model fitting failures abort the run before report replacement.
bounds: Unchanged runtime provider and flow policies, including 64 nodes/edges, support 16, exact rational digit bound 256 and four iterations. Unavailable flow attempts are reproduced by runtime replay; independent NetworkX certifies successful trajectories, not the runtime digit-limit failure itself.
controls: Unit-half must reproduce all D6.3 geometry and model summaries exactly. Doubling every initial length must preserve all normalized edge fields, terminal geometry and model summaries exactly. Source/target/group identities and B/S columns are unchanged in every variant.

independent.scope: Dijkstra distances and integer-scaled transport independently replay every successful flow state. Separate Bellman-Ford/pair aggregation and joint-intercept ridge verify feature joins, nested fits and exact comparisons. The external algorithm is independent; the repository wrapper is not independent scientific review.
